metadata.title: Claude, Guideline Generation.
metadata.purpose: Answer whether a Claude brand voice guideline comes from Claude's own taste in good writing -- or something narrower. Lands the carry-out that guideline-generation is a fixed extraction run on your source material that returns the same patterns every time, and stops the moment you ask it to judge rather than extract.
metadata.source_note: Source sheet has an unfilled template gap (literal '>' in several narration strings and B03.body) -- a batch build defect, not missing content: the description sentence it should have interpolated is intact elsewhere in the same sheet (B00.output[1] and BVDT.artifactLines[1]: 'Generates brand voice guidelines from source materials.'). This redo fills every gap with that source-confirmed sentence -- no external file read or invented. Facts preserved: guideline-generation is a folder (SKILL.md + references/, 2 files) Claude reads before acting; it generates brand voice guidelines from source materials; Claude reads the Steps section and executes each step in order, linearly; same input produces the same output every run, bounded by what SKILL.md specifies. Register re-registered Teardown -> Plain; source's B03/BVDT design-tell verdict became a plain mechanism + both-directions beat; a wrong-guess beat and an anchor (ten blog posts: read -> extract -> structure -> return) were added per hai-simple's Phase 1 structure, since the source's Teardown shape carried neither.

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes a brand voice guideline comes from Claude's own taste in writing. It doesn't — it comes from a spec that pulls patterns from your own samples. So how does that work?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('taste' -> 'your samples') is visible on a late frame, fully settled before the beat ends.

beats.narration_text: The natural guess is that a Claude brand voice guideline comes from good literary taste — an editor's ear for what your writing should sound like. But the skill doesn't work that way. It's a specification: a written instruction set that tells Claude exactly how to read your source material and pull out the same kind of patterns every time, run the same way no matter whose writing it is. Ask it to judge whether your voice is any good, and there's no step written for that.

shot.new_visual_element: A 'Claude's taste' figure with a scattered thought-bubble, struck through; a spec card (read SKILL.md / execute steps / return the guideline) lit instead

production_viz.label: Claude's taste, struck -- the spec, lit
production_viz.mechanic: Left: a figure icon labelled 'CLAUDE'S TASTE' beside a thought-bubble of scattered decision marks. Right: a numbered card labelled 'THE SPEC' listing three steps: read SKILL.md, execute steps in order, return the guideline. The taste side dims and gets a terracotta strike; the spec card stays lit. A final line reads 'judge the voice? -- no step' and the figure does not reach for it.

beats.narration_text: What the skill actually does: read the source material, extract the patterns the file defines, structure them into a guideline, and return the document. Watch the anchor: ten blog posts, handed over for a brand voice guideline. They get read, run through the same extraction steps, structured into sections, and returned as one guideline — tone, word choices, and examples pulled straight from those ten posts.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR -- a 'ten blog posts' token traveling read -> extract -> structure -> returned

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR -- one source, four stops
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. Four stacked cards labelled 'READ', 'EXTRACT', 'STRUCTURE', 'RETURN'. A single highlighted token 'TEN BLOG POSTS' travels down through all four cards in turn, each lighting terracotta as it arrives. At the bottom, beside the RETURN card, a small note reads 'one guideline document' and the token halts there. THIS EXACT COMPOSITION RETURNS, CONDENSED, AT B03.

beats.narration_text: That guideline holds because the extraction ran the same way every time — feed the same ten posts through twice, and the tone notes, the word choices, and the examples come back identical. But ask something outside that — say, whether the voice in those posts is actually a good one — and there's nothing tailored to reach for; the skill stops exactly where its extraction steps stop.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS, condensed; splits into 'run twice -- same guideline' and 'any good? -- no step'

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS -- run twice, or stops there
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 COMPOSITION RETURNS, condensed to a small resting row (EXTRACT / STRUCTURE / RETURN). It shrinks and slides up. Two cards fade in beneath: left reads 'RUN TWICE' then 'SAME GUIDELINE' with a checkmark, labelled 'same input, same guideline' (holds); right reads 'IS IT GOOD?' then a struck-through 'JUDGE?', labelled 'stops where the file does' (flips).

beats.narration_text: A Claude brand voice guideline isn't its own taste in good writing — it's a fixed extraction run on your source material that returns the same patterns every time, and it stops the moment you ask it to judge rather than extract.

props.sparkLine: Extracted from your samples, not taste.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Hand me a handful of your own writing samples, and run the guideline-generation skill: read them, extract the patterns, and return a brand voice guideline. Then ask me whether that voice is actually a good one, and see whether I invent an opinion, or tell you plainly that's outside what the file covers. Liam, in for Bear.
